paper_metadata.title: High-strength and thermally stable TiB2-modified Al-Mn-Mg-Er-Zr alloy fabricated via selective laser melting
paper_metadata.journal: International Journal of Minerals, Metallurgy and Materials

In this study, TiB2-modified Al–Mn–Mg–Er–Zr alloy was produced via SLM.
For the as-built TiB2/Al–Mn–Mg–Er–Zr alloy, the UTS, YS, and elongation are (507 ± 8), (342 ± 6) MPa, and (13.6 ± 1.4)%, respectively.
Compared to the SLM-fabricated Al–Mn–Mg–Er–Zr, the addition of TiB2 nanoparticles leads to a reduction in the grain size (Fig. 6(a) and (b)).
After 400°C-4 h aging treatment, the alloy demonstrates exceptional strength properties, including UTS of (512 ± 6), YS of (374 ± 1) MPa, and elongation of (6.2 ± 0.5)%.
Even after subjecting the alloy to aging treatment at 400°C for 18 h, the average grain size remained virtually unchanged (Fig. 6).
The powder with a composition of 6.01wt% Mn, 2.74wt% Mg, 0.86wt% Er, 0.52wt% Zr, and Al balance, was prepared by a nitrogen-protected atomization system.
Nano-TiB2/Al–Mn–Mg–Er–Zr composite (2.00wt% TiB2) powder was blended by mechanical mixing for 12 h at a speed of 200 r/min. The mean size of TiB2 particles was 50 nm.

During the SLM process, laser power of 250 and 350 W, spot size of 70 μm, layer thickness of 30 μm, hatch spacing of 70 μm, scanning speed of 800–1200 mm/s, and rotation angle of 67° were used. Before the SLM process, the platform was preheated to a temperature of 100°C.

evidence.quote: The bright white nano-scaled particles with spherical shapes were uniformly distributed in the sample. Furthermore, some blocky agglomerated particles with micro-scaled could also be found. These particles could be proved to be TiB2 according to EDX mapping (Fig. 8(b)).

Only a small number of spherical pores were observed in the sample, which is consistent with the OM results (Fig. 4).

attributes.morphology: fine equiaxed grains at molten pool boundaries and coarse columnar grains within molten pool

evidence.quote: The SLM-fabricated TiB2/Al–Mn–Mg–Er–Zr alloy demonstrated a bimodal microstructure. The fine equiaxed grains were observed along the boundaries of the molten pool, while the coarse columnar grains were present within the molten pool. The mean grain size was about 4.15 µm.
